name: Metronidazole
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Metronidazole is metabolized in the liver; kidney impairment does not change its own kinetics, but its hydroxy and acetate metabolites build up in kidney failure. The US label gives no kidney dose change. Hemodialysis removes 40% to 65% of a dose, so give it after the session or add a supplement; CAPD removes little and needs no change. Severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh C) needs a 50% dose cut.
kidney_function_basis: Label PK uses CrCl (mL/min); no kidney bands.
chip: No kidney change; dose after HD

No dose change: kidney impairment does not alter single-dose metronidazole kinetics (label). In end-stage kidney disease, peak levels of hydroxy-metronidazole were 2 times and of metronidazole acetate 5 times normal (label PK). Because metabolites accumulate in end-stage kidney disease, monitoring for metronidazole-associated adverse events is recommended (label).

hd.text: Hemodialysis (4 to 8 hours) removes 40% to 65% of a dose. If dosing cannot be separated from the session, consider a supplemental dose after hemodialysis (label).

pd.text: No dose change on CAPD; a 7.5-hour peritoneal dialysis removed about 10% of a dose (label).

crrt.text: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
crrt.short: No CRRT data in cited sources

dialyzable: Hemodialysis: yes (40% to 65% of a dose per 4- to 8-hour session, by membrane and duration). Peritoneal dialysis: little (about 10%) (label). Under 20% protein bound.
monitoring: Neurologic symptoms (encephalopathy, cerebellar signs, seizures, peripheral or optic neuropathy, aseptic meningitis); liver function in hepatic impairment; INR with warfarin; lithium and creatinine with lithium (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Intra-abdominal infections in infants under 4 months; other indications in adults (IV label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Under 4 months, intra-abdominal infection: loading dose 15 mg/kg, then 7.5 mg/kg starting 24 hours later, every 12 hours (postmenstrual age 23 to under 34 weeks), every 8 hours (34 to 40 weeks) or every 6 hours (over 40 to 48 weeks) (label Table 2).
